key_insight: Large language models can learn grammar-adaptation patterns from past metamodel–grammar version pairs and automatically apply accurate grammar updates after metamodel evolution, handling complex cases that rule-based approaches struggle with.
problem_solved: Automates the tedious, error-prone task of adapting grammars to remain consistent with evolving metamodels—reducing manual effort and overcoming limitations of rule-based partial automation in complex grammar scenarios.
method: Learn adaptation mappings from historical pairs of metamodel and grammar versions (training or in-context examples) so the model infers edit patterns.
Use an LLM (prompting or fine-tuning) to generate concrete grammar transformations or edit scripts for new metamodel changes, with automated validation checks.
Evaluate against rule-based baselines on correctness, coverage and manual-effort reduction; optionally include a human-in-the-loop verification step for risky edits.
impact: Enables faster, more reliable maintenance of DSLs and modeling toolchains by reducing manual grammar editing and increasing automation coverage; makes integrating LLM-based automation into model-driven engineering workflows practical for practitioners.
visual_elements: Flowchart: Metamodel change -> LLM-based adaptation -> Updated grammar (highlighting automated steps)
Before/After diff panels showing a concrete grammar fragment pre- and post-adaptation
Bar chart comparing automation rate, correctness, and manual effort between LLM approach and rule-based baselines
Icon set: version-pair dataset, LLM/brain, edit/wrench, verification/checkmark
paper_title: Leveraging LLMs for Grammar Adaptation: A Study on Metamodel-Grammar Co-Evolution
paper_authors: Weixing Zhang, Bowen Jiang, Rahul Sharma, Regina Hebig, Daniel Strüber
